title: Xi-Trump-Putin summit concludes with joint statement warning world bodies to not 'abuse their jurisdiction'

blocks.text: World·Updated
U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese and Russian counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin met for an unprecedented three-way meeting on Thursday, concluding their talks after more than an hour.
Leaders also vow to prevent nuclear proliferation after historic 3-way summit
Trump, Xi, Putin warn ICC, other world bodies not to 'abuse their jurisdiction'

Earlier, the leaders of the world's biggest nuclear powers, sitting at a round table in a villa nestled among wooded hills beside a lake in the southern ‌Chinese city of Shenzhen, described their meeting as a historic moment.
Trump soon left for the Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport, where he engaged in a brief conversation with China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi before departing on Air Force One en route to Washington.
"We are really making history," Trump said at the onset of the trilateral meeting. "The three of us have a great deal to discuss."
"No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement."
Before their meeting, Trump met Xi and Putin separately, referring to both as friends.

China's President Xi Jinping, left, President Donald Trump, right, and Russia's President Vladimir Putin, centtre, hold a trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday. (Andres Martinez Casares/The Associated Press)
Leaders say UN needs reform

A joint statement was released after Xi, Trump and Putin met, in which the leaders "reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought." The countries pledged to hold a dialogue on reducing nuclear risk and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.
Other parts of the joint statement might make the leaders of European Union and NATO countries uneasy.

The three heads of state "concurred that the International Criminal Court (ICC) and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction," and said they were committed to reform of the United Nations so that it "can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security."

The United Nations Security Council is expected to hold another secret ballot this week to pick the next UN chief, ‌but after eight rounds of voting, the council’s five veto-wielding members have not agreed on a successor ahead of Antonio Guterres's last day on Dec. 31. France and Britain are the other two veto powers.

Trump, left, speaks during a meeting with Xi Jinping on Thursday. With Trump on the American side of the table are, from left to right, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller. (Andres Martinez Casares/The Associated Press)

With respect to the ICC, the statement read that the leaders "recognized that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance." Putin faces an international arrest warrant from the ICC over the war in Ukraine.

While other U.S. administrations have criticized the Hague court, the Trump administration has unleashed a suite of sanctions on it, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio saying the U.S. wanted to "dismantle the ICC, piece by piece."

How China is positioning itself as a global leader as it hosts Trump, Putin

blocks.text: Finally, the three countries stressed the importance of stable energy flows and "plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations." Trump's decision to wage war on Iran with Israel on Feb. 28 has led to monthslong issues for commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, raising global oil prices.
Trump said both he and Xi felt strongly about oil having to flow through the Strait of Hormuz. Xi did not mention Ukraine or Iran in any of his remarks during the two-day summit.

Putin said the three countries have "numerous shared interests in the settlement of regional conflicts, including obviously the conflict in Ukraine." Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, a war that has led to significant casualties and exchanged attacks on energy facilities and other infrastructure.
Putin, left, and Xi shake hands after the meeting with Trump. (Sergei Bobylev/The Associated Press)
Trump arrived in China after Xi and Putin delivered pointed speeches denouncing Western trade "protectionism" and sanctions.

During Thursday's APEC proceedings, Xi ​called for "free and open" trade. Western leaders say China's growth model favouring industrial strength over consumers is unfair and creates destabilizing global trade imbalances.
Putin, fresh from a setback in his war against Ukraine after the crippling of a key bridge linking Crimea to Russia, said Russia was key for ⁠food and energy security in the Asia-Pacific.
'A big win for us'

Trump's talks with Xi come after an extension of their trade truce this month, but also amid growing tension over reports of Nvidia chips being diverted to China through Southeast Asia, raising questions about the effectiveness of U.S. export curbs and the future of Chinese access to advanced technology.

Trump downplayed the allegations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a Chinese spy. Trump in the past two years has developed a close relationship with Huang, and both the president and his Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have faced questions over when they knew about the allegations, given weighty decisions that have been made by the White House over export controls on Nvidia chips.

Asked during an interview on Fox News what he hoped to accomplish at a trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin, Trump suggested he had already secured a victory simply in the way he was received in China.

He repeatedly pointed to Xi's unprecedented decision to greet him at the airport, the elaborate military welcome, thousands of spectators and even the seating chart at the banquet that put Trump at the head table as evidence of the strength of their relationship.
"That's a big win for us. It's a big win for China too. We get ​along," Trump said.
With files from CBC News and The Associated Press
